name: Dutch Golden Age interior

influenced_by: Protestant Dutch merchant culture's taste for domestic scenes over religious commissions

garments: black wool and starched white linen (the burgher uniform)

media.title: Johannes Vermeer, Girl with a Pearl Earring (c. 1665)

reacts_against: the large-scale religious and mythological painting that dominated Catholic Europe; a newly Protestant, merchant-funded market favored small domestic scenes instead.

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Genre scenes (domestic life), individual and group portraits, still lifes (vanitas, floral, banquet), landscapes, seascapes
wiki_facts.key_colours: Somber, earthy tones (browns, ochres, grays), masterful use of light and shadow (chiaroscuro), accents of brilliant color
wiki_facts.related_aesthetics: BaroqueDanish Golden AgeFlemish BaroqueNorthern RenaissanceSpanish Golden Age
wiki_facts.key_values: Realism, observation of daily life, Protestant morality, civic pride, prosperity, domesticity, scientific curiosity

findings: dark — about 58% of the measured color across 6 wiki photos is below mid-lightness
mostly muted — about 81% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
